# GARS execution environment — the single definition of how to run a skill.
#
# Source this from every submit.sh:  source "$WS/_system/gars-env.sh"
#
# Why this file exists: the same ~10 lines of setup were previously copy-pasted into every
# submit.sh, in every project, for every sub-stage. They drifted — a salvaged script was found
# still referencing a vendored skills path that no longer existed.
#
# Why absolute paths rather than `conda activate`: activation would work, but stacking two
# environments needs conda's shell hook sourced inside every batch script, which is more moving
# parts and fails differently on nodes where the hook is absent. Absolute paths behave
# identically everywhere, which is what a Slurm script needs.
#
# Why this lives in the workspace and not in $HOME: a workspace is a copy of the template and
# the contracts treat it as self-contained, so copying a workspace carries its environment
# definition. It is versioned in git, so a change is a reviewable commit rather than an
# untracked edit to a home-directory script.

# --- root ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DO NOT substitute $HOME here. On this cluster $HOME (/gpfs/home/<user>) and the group work
# area (/gpfs/data/abl/home/<user>) are DIFFERENT directories with different inodes -- only some
# subtrees, such as install/, are shared via symlink. Using $HOME once pointed the container
# cache at an empty directory, which silently re-pulls all 26 images and looks like the cache
# "stopped working". Set GARS_ROOT explicitly (e.g. in ~/.bashrc) to the root that holds
# install/ -- there is deliberately no default, because any default is someone's home.
GARS_ROOT="${GARS_ROOT:?[gars-env] FATAL: set GARS_ROOT to the root holding install/ (see _references/environment.md)}"

# --- environments -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two, because nextflow and clawbio have conflicting c-ares constraints and cannot be solved
# together. See _references/environment.md.
GARS_BIO="${GARS_BIO:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-bio}"   # clawbio, apptainer, squashfuse
GARS_NXF="${GARS_NXF:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-nxf}"   # nextflow, openjdk 17

# Order matters. gars-nxf first so `java` resolves to its OpenJDK 17 rather than the system
# Java 1.8 — Nextflow locates Java via PATH, and refuses anything below 17.
export PATH="$GARS_NXF/bin:$GARS_BIO/bin:$PATH"
export JAVA_HOME="$GARS_NXF"

# --- caches -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared across projects: container images and the pinned pipeline are immutable and reusable.
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="${APPTAINER_CACHEDIR:-$GARS_ROOT/.apptainer_cache}"
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"
export NXF_HOME="${NXF_HOME:-$GARS_ROOT/.nextflow_gars}"
mkdir -p "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" "$NXF_HOME"

# --- resolved locations -------------------------------------------------------------------
export GARS_PY="$GARS_BIO/bin/python"

# The retired clawbio skills (decision 0029) are resolved for inspection only -- no sub-stage
# invokes them. The literal site-packages path embeds a Python version that changes on any
# environment rebuild, hence the runtime resolution. Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine.
# `|| true` carries this file's own promise ("Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine")
# through a caller's `set -e`: a failed command substitution in an assignment is FATAL under
# -e, and every generated submit.sh runs with -e. The cluster never saw it -- clawbio is
# always installed there; the first host without it (the demo's recording rig) died here
# silently, before the script's first echo.
GARS_SKILLS=$("$GARS_PY" -c "import clawbio, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(clawbio.__file__).parent / 'skills')" 2>/dev/null || true)
export GARS_SKILLS

# GARS-authored wrappers, versioned in this workspace and ours to maintain (decision 0012).
# The workspace's batch executor (decision 0039). Seeded by stage 00; edit it per site.
#
# Required, not optional in spirit: GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never
# runs it in the current process (decision 0027). This file says WHICH scheduler. Delete it
# and the built-in Slurm descriptor below is what you get, byte for byte -- so an existing
# cluster workspace behaves exactly as it always has.
#
# The shape is deliberately narrow -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level `key: value` maps.
# `_system/` is stdlib-only (decision 0011), so this is parsed by a small parser we own, not
# by a YAML library. Do not reach for anchors, multi-line scalars or nested lists.
#
# Three doors, and nothing else:
#   header   the directives block the generated submit.sh opens with
#   submit   the argv that hands that GENERATED script to the scheduler -> a job id
#   status   the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED
#
# `submit_argv` runs the generated `submit.sh` and nothing else. It is not a place to add
# pipeline parameters, environment or wrapper logic: the audited parameter surface is
# `_config/<assay>.yaml`, and bypassing it is the one thing this file must never enable.

# The backend. `slurm` and `local` are built in; any other name means this file supplies the
# whole descriptor. (`local` runs the script detached on this machine and reports its PID --
# it is for testing the submit->status walk without a cluster, never a venue for analyses.)
name: slurm

# The directives block. Available placeholders, and only these:
#   {project} {assay} {substage} {partition} {time} {cpus} {mem}
# compute.partition / time / cpus / mem come from `_config/<assay>.yaml`.
directives:
  - "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}"
  - "#SBATCH --partition={partition}"
  - "#SBATCH --time={time}"
  - "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}"
  - "#SBATCH --mem={mem}"
  - "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out"
  - "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err"

# How a script becomes a job. {script} is the generated submit.sh; it must appear.
submit_argv:
  - sbatch
  - "{script}"

# How the job id is read back out of what submit printed. First capture group wins.
# A quoted value is taken verbatim -- there is no escape processing, so a regex is
# written exactly as a regex, single backslashes and all.
job_id_regex: "Submitted batch job (\d+)"

# How the job is asked after. {job_id} must appear.
status_argv:
  - sacct
  - -j
  - "{job_id}"
  - --format=State
  - --noheader

# This backend's states, mapped onto the closed vocabulary. Closed means closed: a state that
# is not listed here is refused by name rather than guessed at, so an unfamiliar scheduler
# state can never be silently read as success.
status_map:
  PENDING: PENDING
  CONFIGURING: PENDING
  REQUEUED: PENDING
  SUSPENDED: PENDING
  PREEMPTED: PENDING
  RUNNING: RUNNING
  COMPLETING: RUNNING
  RESIZING: RUNNING
  COMPLETED: COMPLETED
  FAILED: FAILED
  CANCELLED: FAILED
  TIMEOUT: FAILED
  NODE_FAIL: FAILED
  OUT_OF_MEMORY: FAILED
  BOOT_FAIL: FAILED
  DEADLINE: FAILED
  REVOKED: FAILED

# The Nextflow executor config this backend pairs with, under `_config/`. The wrapper checks
# it exists and carries no `params` block.
nextflow_config: nextflow.slurm.config

# The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
# property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer. A venue that
# supplies each process's container itself (AWS Batch) sets it to "" (quoted -- a bare
# empty value reads as a section opener in the narrow parser), meaning no -profile.
nextflow_profile: apptainer

234	# --- the three doors ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
235	
236	
237	def _fill(text, fields):
238	    """Substitute the KNOWN {tokens} and leave every other brace alone.
239	
240	    Deliberately not str.format: a descriptor element may legitimately contain literal
241	    braces -- the awsbatch submit argv carries a JSON --container-overrides payload, and
242	    format() reads {"command": ...} as a placeholder named \'"command"\' and crashes. The
243	    descriptor is data, not a template language; only the documented tokens are tokens.
244	    """
245	    for key, value in fields.items():
246	        text = text.replace("{%s}" % key, str(value))
247	    return text
248	
249	
250	def header_lines(config_root, cfg, project, assay, substage, descriptor=None):
251	    """The directives block, rendered. Returns a list of lines with no trailing newlines."""
252	    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
253	    fields = {
254	        "project": project,
255	        "assay": assay,
256	        "substage": str(Path(substage).resolve()),
257	        "partition": cfg.get("compute.partition", "{partition}"),
258	        "time": cfg.get("compute.time", "{time}"),
259	        "cpus": cfg.get("compute.cpus", "{cpus}"),
260	        "mem": cfg.get("compute.mem", "{mem}"),
261	    }
262	    return [_fill(line, fields) for line in descriptor.get("directives") or []]
263	
264	
265	DEFAULT_SUBMIT_NOTE = ("The scheduler snapshots this script at submission: editing it never "
266	                       "affects a queued job.")
267	
268	
269	def submit_note(descriptor):
270	    """The one line the generated submit.sh says about editing itself, per backend."""
271	    return descriptor.get("submit_note") or DEFAULT_SUBMIT_NOTE
272	
273	
274	def config_root_for(path):
275	    """The nearest ancestor that owns `_config/` -- a sub-stage or analysis dir's project.
276	
277	    Walked rather than counted: stage 02 sub-stages sit three levels down and stage 03
278	    analyses two, and a seam that hard-codes either depth breaks the other.
279	    """
280	    here = Path(path).resolve()
281	    for candidate in [here] + list(here.parents):
282	        if (candidate / "_config").is_dir():
283	            return candidate
284	    return here
285	
286	
287	def submit_argv(descriptor, script):
288	    return [_fill(a, {"script": script}) for a in descriptor.get("submit_argv") or []]
289	
290	
291	def status_argv(descriptor, job_id):
292	    return [_fill(a, {"job_id": job_id}) for a in descriptor.get("status_argv") or []]
293	
294	
295	def nextflow_config_path(config_root, descriptor=None):
296	    """The nextflow config file this workspace's executor pairs with, or None.
297	
298	    The descriptor names it (0039); callers must never spell `nextflow.slurm.config`
299	    themselves -- that name is the Slurm default, not a law.
300	    """
301	    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
302	    name = descriptor.get("nextflow_config") or ""
303	    return (Path(config_root) / "_config" / name) if name else None
304	
305	
306	def nextflow_profile(config_root, descriptor=None):
307	    """The -profile the generated submit body passes, '' meaning none."""
308	    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
309	    value = descriptor.get("nextflow_profile")
310	    return SLURM["nextflow_profile"] if value is None else value
311	
312	
313	def submit_command(config_root, script, descriptor=None):
314	    """The literal command line `reproducibility/commands.sh` records for this workspace."""
315	    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
316	    if descriptor.get("name") == "local":
317	        return "python3 %s/_system/executorlib.py submit --workspace %s %s" % (
318	            "$WS", str(config_root), str(script))
319	    argv = submit_argv(descriptor, script)
320	    return " ".join(argv) if argv else str(script)
321	
322	
323	def _local_jobs_dir(config_root):
324	    return Path(config_root) / LOCAL_JOBS_DIR
325	
326	
327	#: The one-liner the `local` backend detaches. The outer shell backgrounds a subshell and
328	#: prints its PID, then exits -- so nothing is left for this process to wait on (no orphaned
329	#: Popen handle, no ResourceWarning) and the job outlives the caller, which is the point.
330	#: The GROUP's own descriptors go to /dev/null, not just each command's: a backgrounded job
331	#: inherits the caller's stdout pipe, and a pipe that stays open is a submit that blocks
332	#: until the job finishes -- which is exactly the thing a scheduler must never do.
333	LOCAL_RUNNER = ('{ bash "$1" >> "$2" 2>&1; echo $? > "$3"; } '
334	                '</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &\necho $!\n')
335	
336	
337	def _local_submit(config_root, script):
338	    """Start the generated script detached; the PID is the job id.
339	
340	    POSIX-only by construction, which is the posture GARS already has. The exit code lands in
341	    a sidecar beside the script so `status` can tell COMPLETED from FAILED once the process
342	    is gone -- a PID alone cannot say how a job ended.
343	    """
344	    script = Path(script).resolve()
345	    jobs = _local_jobs_dir(config_root)
346	    jobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
347	    log = script.parent / (script.name + ".local.log")
348	    exit_file = script.parent / (script.name + ".local.exit")
349	    if exit_file.is_file():
350	        exit_file.unlink()          # a re-submit must never read the previous run's verdict
351	    proc = subprocess.run(

def _fill(text, fields):
    """Substitute the KNOWN {tokens} and leave every other brace alone.

    Deliberately not str.format: a descriptor element may legitimately contain literal
    braces -- the awsbatch submit argv carries a JSON --container-overrides payload, and
    format() reads {"command": ...} as a placeholder named \'"command"\' and crashes. The
    descriptor is data, not a template language; only the documented tokens are tokens.
    """
    for key, value in fields.items():
        text = text.replace("{%s}" % key, str(value))
    return text


def header_lines(config_root, cfg, project, assay, substage, descriptor=None):
    """The directives block, rendered. Returns a list of lines with no trailing newlines."""
    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)
    fields = {
        "project": project,
        "assay": assay,
        "substage": str(Path(substage).resolve()),
        "partition": cfg.get("compute.partition", "{partition}"),
        "time": cfg.get("compute.time", "{time}"),
        "cpus": cfg.get("compute.cpus", "{cpus}"),
        "mem": cfg.get("compute.mem", "{mem}"),
    }
    return [_fill(line, fields) for line in descriptor.get("directives") or []]

                       "affects a queued job.")


def submit_note(descriptor):
    """The one line the generated submit.sh says about editing itself, per backend."""
    return descriptor.get("submit_note") or DEFAULT_SUBMIT_NOTE


def config_root_for(path):
    """The nearest ancestor that owns `_config/` -- a sub-stage or analysis dir's project.

    Walked rather than counted: stage 02 sub-stages sit three levels down and stage 03
    analyses two, and a seam that hard-codes either depth breaks the other.
    """
    here = Path(path).resolve()
    for candidate in [here] + list(here.parents):
        if (candidate / "_config").is_dir():
            return candidate
    return here

    return [_fill(a, {"script": script}) for a in descriptor.get("submit_argv") or []]

    The descriptor names it (0039); callers must never spell `nextflow.slurm.config`
    themselves -- that name is the Slurm default, not a law.

    descriptor = descriptor if descriptor is not None else load(config_root)

    return (Path(config_root) / "_config" / name) if name else None

    return Path(config_root) / LOCAL_JOBS_DIR

#: prints its PID, then exits -- so nothing is left for this process to wait on (no orphaned
#: Popen handle, no ResourceWarning) and the job outlives the caller, which is the point.
#: The GROUP's own descriptors go to /dev/null, not just each command's: a backgrounded job
#: inherits the caller's stdout pipe, and a pipe that stays open is a submit that blocks

LOCAL_RUNNER = ('{ bash "$1" >> "$2" 2>&1; echo $? > "$3"; } '
                '</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &\necho $!\n')


def _local_submit(config_root, script):
    """Start the generated script detached; the PID is the job id.

    POSIX-only by construction, which is the posture GARS already has. The exit code lands in
    a sidecar beside the script so `status` can tell COMPLETED from FAILED once the process
    is gone -- a PID alone cannot say how a job ended.

    script = Path(script).resolve()
    jobs = _local_jobs_dir(config_root)
    jobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if exit_file.is_file():
        exit_file.unlink()          # a re-submit must never read the previous run's verdict

        ["bash", "-c", LOCAL_RUNNER, "gars-local", str(script), str(log), str(exit_file)],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)

    exit_file = Path(json.loads(record.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["exit_file"])

"""PCA of the gene counts, coloured by condition -- implements PLAN.md, Method steps 1-8."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

WS, PROJECT, ANALYSIS = (Path(p).resolve() for p in sys.argv[1:4])
RESULTS = ANALYSIS / "results"
RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def resolve(artifact_type):
    """Method step 1: every input through resolve_artifact.py, never a guessed path."""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(WS / "_system" / "resolve_artifact.py"), "--project", str(PROJECT),
         "--assay", "rnaseq_bulk", "--type", artifact_type],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    hit = out.get("resolved", {}).get(artifact_type)
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not out.get("ok") or not hit or not hit.get("exists"):
        sys.exit("cannot resolve %s: %s" % (artifact_type, json.dumps(out)))
    return PROJECT / hit["resolved"]


# Step 2: load inputs and check the sample sets agree.
counts = pd.read_csv(resolve("counts_gene"), sep="\t")
counts = counts.drop(columns=["gene_name"]).set_index("gene_id")
design = pd.read_csv(resolve("design")).set_index("sample_id")
if set(design.index) != set(counts.columns):
    sys.exit("design samples %s != counts samples %s"
             % (sorted(design.index), sorted(counts.columns)))
counts = counts[design.index]

# Step 3: round length-scaled counts, drop all-zero genes.
counts = counts.round().astype(int)
counts = counts.loc[counts.sum(axis=1) > 0]

# Step 4: blind VST with pydeseq2 (samples x genes).
dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T, metadata=design, design="~condition")
dds.vst(use_design=False)
vst = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["vst_counts"], index=counts.columns, columns=counts.index)

# Step 5: top 500 most variable genes (all if fewer).
top = vst.var(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:500]
X = vst[top]

# Step 6: PCA, centred not scaled.
n = min(X.shape)
pca = PCA(n_components=n)
scores = pca.fit_transform(X - X.mean(axis=0))
pcs = ["PC%d" % (i + 1) for i in range(n)]

# Step 7: tables.
coords = pd.DataFrame(scores, index=X.index, columns=pcs)
coords = design[["condition", "group", "replicate"]].join(coords)
coords.index.name = "sample_id"
coords.to_csv(RESULTS / "pca_coordinates.csv")
ratio = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
pd.DataFrame({"component": pcs, "variance_explained": ratio,
              "cumulative": np.cumsum(ratio)}).to_csv(
    RESULTS / "pca_variance_explained.csv", index=False)

# Step 8: PC1 vs PC2, coloured by condition, labelled by sample_id.
palette = ["#1f77b4", "#d62728", "#2ca02c", "#9467bd"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.5))
for i, (cond, sub) in enumerate(coords.groupby("condition", sort=True)):
    ax.scatter(sub["PC1"], sub["PC2"], s=60, color=palette[i % len(palette)], label=cond,
               edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
    for sid, row in sub.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(sid, (row["PC1"], row["PC2"]), xytext=(5, 4),
                    textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%% variance)" % (100 * ratio[0]))
ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%% variance)" % (100 * ratio[1]))
ax.set_title("Sample PCA (VST, top %d variable genes)" % len(top))
ax.legend(title="condition", frameon=False)
ax.grid(alpha=0.3, zorder=0)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_pc1_pc2.png", dpi=300)
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_pc1_pc2.pdf")
print("wrote", sorted(p.name for p in RESULTS.iterdir()))

design = pd.read_csv(resolve("design")).set_index("sample_id")
if set(design.index) != set(counts.columns):
    sys.exit("design samples %s != counts samples %s"
             % (sorted(design.index), sorted(counts.columns)))
counts = counts[design.index]

# Step 3: round length-scaled counts, drop all-zero genes.
counts = counts.round().astype(int)
counts = counts.loc[counts.sum(axis=1) > 0]

# Step 4: blind VST with pydeseq2 (samples x genes).
dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts.T, metadata=design, design="~condition")
dds.vst(use_design=False)
vst = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["vst_counts"], index=counts.columns, columns=counts.index)

# Step 5: top 500 most variable genes (all if fewer).
top = vst.var(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:500]
X = vst[top]

# Step 6: PCA, centred not scaled.
n = min(X.shape)
pca = PCA(n_components=n)
scores = pca.fit_transform(X - X.mean(axis=0))
pcs = ["PC%d" % (i + 1) for i in range(n)]

# Step 7: tables.
coords = pd.DataFrame(scores, index=X.index, columns=pcs)
coords = design[["condition", "group", "replicate"]].join(coords)
coords.index.name = "sample_id"
coords.to_csv(RESULTS / "pca_coordinates.csv")
ratio = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
pd.DataFrame({"component": pcs, "variance_explained": ratio,
              "cumulative": np.cumsum(ratio)}).to_csv(
    RESULTS / "pca_variance_explained.csv", index=False)

# Step 8: PC1 vs PC2, coloured by condition, labelled by sample_id.
palette = ["#1f77b4", "#d62728", "#2ca02c", "#9467bd"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4.5))
for i, (cond, sub) in enumerate(coords.groupby("condition", sort=True)):
    ax.scatter(sub["PC1"], sub["PC2"], s=60, color=palette[i % len(palette)], label=cond,
               edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
    for sid, row in sub.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(sid, (row["PC1"], row["PC2"]), xytext=(5, 4),
                    textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%% variance)" % (100 * ratio[0]))
ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%% variance)" % (100 * ratio[1]))
ax.set_title("Sample PCA (VST, top %d variable genes)" % len(top))
ax.legend(title="condition", frameon=False)
ax.grid(alpha=0.3, zorder=0)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_pc1_pc2.png", dpi=300)
fig.savefig(RESULTS / "pca_pc1_pc2.pdf")
print("wrote", sorted(p.name for p in RESULTS.iterdir()))
